title: What If a Desert Had No Water?

voice.direction: A calm guide stepping back from one cup to the whole desert. Hushed and curious on the hook ('worth more than gold'), matter-of-fact on the price, then three quick, dry observations (houses, rations, roads), a low reveal on 'One family holds the keys', a beat of quiet menace on 'never needed an army', warm and practical on the lesson, conversational on the CTA. No trailer voice.

lines.text: How does a civilization survive where water is worth more than gold?
In Sarrun, one cup is a day's wage.
Houses turn inward, catching every drop of dew.
Rations are measured. Spilling is a crime.
Roads bend from well to well, never straight.
And every well is locked. One family holds the keys.
Make anything scarce, and whoever holds it rules the region.
Follow for more ways to turn geography into storytelling.

shots.purpose: Stop the scroll on the whole episode in one object: a single cup of water on a desert ledge, with gold coins tossed beside it like small change.
shots.visual: Close-up: a clay cup filled to the brim on sun-baked sandstone, five gold coins scattered in the dust beside it, a mud-brick city out of focus behind. Title 'WATER, WORTH MORE / than gold.'
shots.camera: Slow pull back (1.12 to 1.06): the first step of the episode-long pull-back.

layers.foreground: cup and coins on the ledge

shots.lighting: Harsh late desert sun from the left, long cup shadow; top scrim for the title.
shots.imagePrompt: Vertical 9:16 cinematic fantasy documentary still. Close-up of a single small unglazed clay cup filled to the brim with clear, glistening water, standing on a weathered sandstone ledge in the exact centre of the frame. Beside the cup, a small careless scatter of five old gold coins lies in the sand dust, catching the light, clearly worth less than the water. A few drops of condensation run down the cup. Behind, softly out of focus, a sun-bleached desert city of flat-roofed mud-brick houses and pale dunes under a hazy white-gold sky. Harsh late-afternoon desert sunlight from the left, long shadow of the cup across the ledge, heat shimmer. The upper third of the frame is calm hazy sky with nothing in it. Shallow depth of field. shots.transition: Hard cut on 'In' (same plate, the pull-back continues).
shots.music: E minor add9, open and dry: a question in the heat.

shots.purpose: Name the place and put a price on the cup: in Sarrun, one cup costs a day's work.
shots.visual: Same cup; an ember survey ring closes around it while the coins sit outside the ring. Tag: SARRUN / one cup, one day's wage.
shots.onScreenText: Tag 'SARRUN' + 'one cup, one day's wage'; ember ring around the cup.
shots.transition: Hard cut on 'Houses': the cup shrinks into the cistern of a courtyard house.
shots.music: C major 7, sparse: the price of a cup.

shots.purpose: Architecture: scarcity turns every house inward. Roofs slope to a cistern, walls have no outside windows, nets catch the dew.
shots.visual: Bird's-eye view of a windowless mud-brick courtyard house; the cup from the hook shrinks into its cistern. Water-blue dashed lines run from every roof spout to the cistern.

layers.background: neighbouring roofs, wind tower, open sand

shots.lighting: Low golden morning light, long shadows.
shots.imagePrompt: Vertical 9:16 cinematic fantasy documentary still. A high bird's-eye view looking down into a desert courtyard house built to waste no water. Thick windowless outer walls of tan mud brick face the empty sand outside; everything turns inward to a small shaded square courtyard in the centre of the frame. In the middle of the courtyard, a round stone cistern mouth with a wooden lid. Flat roofs slope gently inward toward the courtyard with clay gutters and spouts all pointing to the cistern. A tall square wind tower rises at one corner. Fine pale nets are stretched on wooden frames on the roof to catch dew. A potted fig tree and a few herbs in the courtyard shade; one small figure in a pale robe, seen from above at a modest distance, lifting the cistern lid. Neighbouring flat-roofed houses of the same kind fill the edges of the frame. Early morning low golden light, long soft shadows, dust haze. Painterly realism, atmospheric perspective, 35mm anamorphic look, soft film grain, original architecture and clothing. No text, no letters, no signage, no logos, no watermark.

shots.onScreenText: Tag 'ARCHITECTURE' + 'turned inward'; water-blue lines from every spout to the cistern.
shots.transition: Hard cut on 'Rations' down into the street.
shots.music: A minor over a 66 bpm pulse: the system begins.

shots.purpose: Law: water is rationed by measure at a locked public spout, and wasting it is a crime.
shots.visual: Narrow street; a guard pours one exact ration from a bronze ladle at a padlocked spout while a queue waits with jars. Ember ring on the ladle; rust kicker.

layers.background: awnings and the bright end of the street

shots.lighting: Hard midday light, deep blue shadows.
shots.imagePrompt: Vertical 9:16 cinematic fantasy documentary still. A public water stand in a narrow sun-baked desert street of a mud-brick city. In the centre of the frame, a heavy carved stone basin set into a wall, with a single bronze spout locked by an iron bar and a big padlock. A stern guard in a dark indigo robe and turban stands beside it holding a bronze measuring ladle over a clay jar, pouring one exact ration. A quiet line of townspeople in pale dusty robes waits with clay jars and waterskins along the wall, seen from behind or in profile at a modest distance, faces shaded. On the dry paving stones in the foreground a single small dark splash of spilled water. Harsh midday light, deep blue shadows, dust in the air, awnings of faded cloth overhead. Painterly realism, atmospheric perspective, 35mm anamorphic look, soft film grain, original architecture and clothing. No text, no letters, no signage, no logos, no watermark.

shots.onScreenText: Tag 'LAW' + 'every drop counted'; ember ring on the measuring ladle.
shots.transition: Hard cut on 'Roads' up to the dunes.
shots.music: F major 7 over the pulse: order.

shots.purpose: Transport: routes are set by water, not distance. The caravan bends from well to well; the straight line would kill it.
shots.visual: Aerial dunes; an amber dashed route traces the caravan's bending path through the oasis wells, water rings mark the wells, and a rust dashed straight line is struck out.
shots.camera: Slow push (1.04 to 1.08), frame raised so the lower well stays above the platform buttons.
shots.lighting: Late golden light, long blue dune shadows.
shots.imagePrompt: Vertical 9:16 cinematic fantasy documentary still. A high aerial view over an immense rolling sea of pale golden sand dunes at late afternoon. A long camel caravan of small figures winds through the dunes along a wandering, zig-zagging path that clearly bends from one tiny oasis well to the next: three small round stone well-heads, each with a little ring of palms, placed at different points down the frame, the first at the bottom, one in the middle left, one in the upper right. The caravan is between the bottom well and the middle one, following the curve. Nothing else but sand between the wells. Long blue shadows on the dune ridges, warm haze toward the horizon, open pale sky in the upper fifth of the frame. Painterly realism, atmospheric perspective, 35mm anamorphic look, soft film grain. No text, no letters, no signage, no logos, no watermark.
shots.videoPrompt: (Not used.) The caravan plodding along the curve, sand blowing off the ridges, 3 seconds
shots.onScreenText: Tag 'ROADS' + 'well to well'; amber route through water-ringed wells; rust straight line struck out.
shots.transition: Hard cut on 'And': the dune photo shrinks onto its route on the region map.
shots.music: D minor 9, pulse 72 bpm: the long road.

shots.purpose: Power, the full pull-back: the region as a system of wells, every one locked and tethered to one family in Sarrun. Its control spreads over the whole map without a single army.
shots.visual: The caravan photo shrinks onto its route on a desert map. Dunes, eight wells linked by caravan routes, Sarrun in the middle; padlocks snap onto every well; ember threads run from each well to the city; then Sarrun's amber wash floods the region.
shots.lighting: Series map look: parchment ink on dark paper.
shots.onScreenText: Map label 'Sarrun'; padlocks on all eight wells; threads to the city; amber control wash.
shots.transition: Dissolve (0.6 s) back to the cup.
shots.music: C to B major (the dominant): control tightening, holding its breath.

shots.purpose: The lesson, back where it started: the whole system was inside one cup. Make anything scarce and power gathers around whoever holds it.
shots.visual: Dissolve back to the cup; the water glows ember. Lesson lockup: MAKE ANYTHING SCARCE / whoever holds it, rules.
shots.onScreenText: 'MAKE ANYTHING SCARCE' (amber kicker) + 'whoever holds it, rules.' (ember serif italic).
shots.transition: Dissolve (0.6 s) to the same cup at dusk.
shots.music: E major with bells: the answer.

shots.purpose: Follow CTA over the same cup at dusk, the city lighting up behind it; ends on the hook's first frame for a loop.
shots.visual: The cup at dusk, its water catching the last light, windows lit in the city behind. Full logo, Episode 08 / 50, the CTA in large serif type, 'Follow' pill.
shots.camera: Settles back toward the hook's first framing (1.05 to 1.12).
shots.lighting: Dusk grade with city lights in code; last 0.6 s cross-fades to the sunlit first frame.

shots.music: A to E major, warm; fades fully before the last frame.

lesson: Scarcity reorganizes a whole society (houses, laws, roads) around one resource, and power gathers around whoever controls it. Make something scarce in your world, then decide who holds it.

music.key: E minor, resolving to E major
